segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The sound didn't come from the door. It came from the snowy scrap heaps all around you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Snow began sliding down the piles of rusted gears. Crawling out from beneath broken clock towers and hollow brass bells were dozens of wooden figures.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They weren't Nutcrackers. They were Scrap Goblins—two-foot-tall figures carved out of rough, weathered cedar and pine. They had long, spindly wooden arms with carved claws, pointed wooden noses, and hollow red-glass eyes that flickered like dying embers.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Their wooden jaws clicked open and shut in rhythmic, unnerving synchronization:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip whispered, his British accent evaporating in a microsecond.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Those... those do not look like diplomatic welcoming dignitaries.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the wooden goblins hissed in scratchy, wooden voices like sandpaper rubbing on bark.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: INTRUDERS AT THE THRESHOLD! CHOP! CHOP! SPLINTER THEM TO KINDLING!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Dozens of them scrambled down the junk heaps, surrounding the balloon ledge!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you yell, backing toward the iron door.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan scrambled out of the basket to stand beside you, his massive muscular body shaking like a bowl of jelly.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I-I-I don't like their faces! Why are their teeth so pointy?! I am having a major emotional setback!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You examine the heavy iron door behind you. Beside the latch is a brass puzzle-dial with three symbols: a Cog, a Bell, and a Key. To open the door, you need to solve the combination, but the wooden horde is twenty feet away and closing fast!
